name: com.marketinque/launch-plan
title: marketinque — launch plan & backlink index
description: A 498-step SaaS launch plan and 958 backlink sources as tools an agent reads, acts on and records.

tools.name: whoami
tools.description: Which mode this connection is in — anonymous (read-only) or a project — and what that unlocks.

tools.name: join_waitlist
tools.description: Put the founder on the marketinque waitlist for a project (the idea queue, kit, dossier, signals, nightly routine — free for now, opening by waitlist). Call ONLY after the founder gave you their email and said yes in this session; `confirmed` attests that. One email, no spam; they can unsubscribe from any mail.

email.description: The founder’s email, as they gave it.

product_url.description: Their product, so the invitation can refer to it.

confirmed.description: True only if the founder explicitly agreed to join, in this session.

tools.name: get_plan
tools.description: The launch plan. With no `node`: the outline — phases and objectives with step counts. With `node` (a phase or objective slug): every step under it, with status and whether it is unlocked. Anonymous callers pass `done`/`not_applicable`/`traits`; a project uses its own.

node.description: A phase or objective slug from the outline, e.g. "p2" or "p2-dr-assets".

traits.description: Product traits that decide which steps apply (b2b, b2c, ai-native, dev-tool, no-code, mcp, has-integrations, eu-traffic, mobile-app); omit for the generic plan. Free tier only; a project's saved traits are used instead.

done.description: Step slugs already done — the "done" list of marketinque.json. Free tier only; a project's own ticks are used instead and this is ignored.

not_applicable.description: Step slugs the founder ruled out — the "not_applicable" list of marketinque.json. Free tier only; ignored for a project.

tools.name: search_knowledge
tools.description: Search the library: the source-checked claims behind the launch plan's statistics, and (with a `query`) the wiki topics, plays and defined terms that match. Each claim says what kind it is (standard, evidence, practitioner-consensus, our-take), how strong it is and why, when it was last checked, the sources it cites with how well each was read, and the plan steps that rely on it. `topics`, `plays` and `terms` are short records: open one with get_topic, get_play or define_term. Use it before quoting a number from the plan or from a marketing article. With no filters it returns the strongest claims first and no topics, plays or terms; with a `query` it matches every word in the claim, its sources and its correction note, and in a topic, play or term. Read-only; no side effects.

query.description: Words to look for, e.g. "paywall", "Product Hunt", "dunning".

step.description: Only claims that back this plan step slug, e.g. "p3-cnv-trial".

tools.name: get_step
tools.description: One plan step in full: title, detail, the target URL where it happens, the play it follows (its URL and its text: summary, pattern, steps, constraints), the prerequisite slugs and whether they are met (unlocked), how it verifies (self, evidence URL or an automatic signal), minutes and cost, and founder_steps when part of the step is the founder’s own (an account, a handle): the exact page and what to do there, to hand over rather than do. Read it before working a step that next_steps or get_plan returned; the slug comes from those. Read-only; no side effects.

slug.description: The step slug exactly as get_plan or next_steps returned it, e.g. "p2-dest-alternatives".

done.description: Step slugs already done — the "done" list of marketinque.json. Free tier only; a project's own ticks are used instead and this is ignored.

not_applicable.description: Step slugs the founder ruled out — the "not_applicable" list of marketinque.json. Free tier only; ignored for a project.

traits.description: Product traits that decide which steps apply (b2b, b2c, ai-native, dev-tool, no-code, mcp, has-integrations, eu-traffic, mobile-app); omit for the generic plan. Free tier only; a project's saved traits are used instead.

tools.name: get_topic
tools.description: One wiki topic (a subject a founder looks up, e.g. "backlinks-and-directories", "retention-and-churn"): its two-sentence summary, every plan step it gathers in plan order grouped by objective (slug, title, detail, time), and for the topics with a written guide the 40–60 word answer it leads with (in_short), its question-shaped "Do it" sections with their steps in reading order (do_it; a section can name a step from outside the topic) and its FAQ; the plays that explain how, the source-checked claims with their sources and how well each was read, and the related topics. The same content as /wiki/<topic> and /wiki/<topic>.md. Read-only; no side effects.

slug.description: The topic slug: first-10-customers, cold-outreach, activation-and-onboarding, reviews-and-social-proof, product-hunt-and-launches, backlinks-and-directories, ai-search-visibility, technical-seo-and-indexing, content-and-seo, programmatic-seo, reddit-and-communities, pricing-and-payments, retention-and-churn, channel-testing-and-attribution, paid-acquisition, founder-brand-and-pr, email-and-newsletters, partnerships-and-referrals, mobile-apps-and-stores, sales-assist-and-new-segments, positioning-and-conversion, delegation-and-hiring.

tools.name: get_play
tools.description: One marketing play from the library in full: its type, summary, the reusable pattern, its own steps (or a note that the channel’s standard steps apply), constraints, who it suits, what it costs, its standing (backed: a platform doc, law, study, dataset or tool doc was read, or a claim supports it; practitioner: only posts, threads or vendor material; our-idea: no source), each source with how well it was read, the wiki topics that list it and the plan steps that follow it. The slug comes from search_plays, get_topic, get_step or search_knowledge. Read-only; no side effects.

tools.name: search_plays
tools.description: Search the library of reusable marketing plays (product-agnostic patterns such as a Product Hunt campaign or a Reddit origin-story post). Ranked: whole-word matches of `query`, title hits first; when no play matches every word, the plays matching most of them. Narrow with `type` (channel), `best_for` (audience), `traits` (the plan traits, mapped to audiences) and `funnel_stage`. With no query, library order (strongest first within a type). Each result: slug, title, type, summary, cost, standing, best_for and funnel_stage; open one with get_play. For "what should I do next", whats_next picks for the product’s stage. Read-only.

query.description: Words to look for, e.g. "launch", "unlinked mention", "newsletter swap".

best_for.description: Only plays that suit one of these audiences.

traits.description: Product traits that decide which steps apply (b2b, b2c, ai-native, dev-tool, no-code, mcp, has-integrations, eu-traffic, mobile-app); omit for the generic plan. Free tier only; a project's saved traits are used instead.

funnel_stage.description: Only plays for this funnel stage.

tools.name: define_term
tools.description: The short definition of a marketing term from the library: the 28 glossary terms (MQL, CAC, dark funnel…), the 19 marketing disciplines and the 9 funnel frameworks (AIDA, AARRR, the flywheel…). Exact name or slug matches come first, then partial ones. Each match has its kind, definition, page URL and related pages. Read-only; no side effects.

tools.name: next_steps
tools.description: The next unlocked, unstarted steps in tree order, and a sprint packed into `minutes`. Each step says its impact (1–3), whether it is on the core path, who can do it (agent, agent-drafts, founder) and whether it repeats. `core_only` keeps the minimum path; `who: "agent"` gives the batch an agent can finish alone. `this_week` lists recurring steps that are due again. Anonymous callers pass `done`/`not_applicable` (from marketinque.json) and `traits`; a project uses its own.

minutes.description: Time available now; the sprint is packed into it (default 120).

limit.description: How many next steps to list (default 8).

checkable_only.description: Only steps with a target to record or an automatic check.

core_only.description: Only steps on the core path: the smallest set that still works.

who.description: agent: steps an agent can finish alone · agent-drafts: those plus steps it prepares for the founder to send · founder: only the founder’s own.

last_done.description: Free tier: when each recurring step was last done, { "<slug>": "YYYY-MM-DD" } — the "last_done" map of marketinque.json. Steps that repeat come due again from this date. A project uses its own dates.

traits.description: Product traits that decide which steps apply (b2b, b2c, ai-native, dev-tool, no-code, mcp, has-integrations, eu-traffic, mobile-app); omit for the generic plan. Free tier only; a project's saved traits are used instead.

done.description: Step slugs already done — the "done" list of marketinque.json. Free tier only; a project's own ticks are used instead and this is ignored.

not_applicable.description: Step slugs the founder ruled out — the "not_applicable" list of marketinque.json. Free tier only; ignored for a project.

tools.name: whats_next
tools.description: Use this when asked "what should I do next?" or "give me the next working idea". Works out the product’s stage (pass `stage`, or it is read from the plan); with no project, pass `product_url` and the site is checked first so what it already does is skipped; then returns the three best next steps for that stage, each with why now, how to do it (the play’s steps or the step’s own how-to), minutes, and how you will know it is done; one unfinished ship-ready basic beside them; and three library plays that suit the stage and audience. next_steps is the plain checklist in plan order; this is the recommendation. Read-only.

stage.description: pre-launch · no-users (live, nobody uses it) · users-not-paying · first-customers (1–9 paying) · growing (10+ paying) · scaling. Omit to read it from the plan.

product_url.description: Free tier: the product’s site. It is read with the free launch report (cached for a day), so steps the site already proves are skipped and its traits are suggested. Ignored for a project, which uses its own plan.

traits.description: Product traits that decide which steps apply (b2b, b2c, ai-native, dev-tool, no-code, mcp, has-integrations, eu-traffic, mobile-app); omit for the generic plan. Free tier only; a project's saved traits are used instead.

done.description: Step slugs already done — the "done" list of marketinque.json. Free tier only; a project's own ticks are used instead and this is ignored.

not_applicable.description: Step slugs the founder ruled out — the "not_applicable" list of marketinque.json. Free tier only; ignored for a project.

last_done.description: Free tier: when each recurring step was last done, { "<slug>": "YYYY-MM-DD" } — the "last_done" map of marketinque.json. Steps that repeat come due again from this date. A project uses its own dates.

tools.name: do_marketing
tools.description: Call this FIRST when asked to "do my marketing", "automate user acquisition", "grow this", or to run the daily marketing routine. It returns the run sheet for the product’s stage: the recurring work due this week, the steps you can finish alone (packed into `minutes`), the ones to draft for the founder up to the send button, the founder’s own list, what to ask about past work, and the order to do it all in, with the rules for sending. `mode: "unattended"` is for a scheduled run with nobody there: no questions, no changes to the product, drafts go to the queue. Read-only; the work is done with the other tools it names.

mode.description: attended (default): the founder is here. unattended: a scheduled run; prepare and queue only.

ship.description: true only when the founder set this run up to ship approved work to their own site from this repository (commit, push, deploy, check live). An unattended run without it changes nothing in the product.

post.description: Networks this run may post APPROVED items to from the founder’s own accounts. Only those the founder named when they set the run up; omit otherwise.

submit_forms.description: true only when the founder set this run up to submit directory listings they approved one by one, on forms that need no account.

minutes.description: Time for the steps you do alone (default 120 attended, 60 unattended).

stage.description: The product’s stage, when known. A project uses its saved stage; omit to read it from the plan.

traits.description: Product traits that decide which steps apply (b2b, b2c, ai-native, dev-tool, no-code, mcp, has-integrations, eu-traffic, mobile-app); omit for the generic plan. Free tier only; a project's saved traits are used instead.

done.description: Step slugs already done — the "done" list of marketinque.json. Free tier only; a project's own ticks are used instead and this is ignored.

not_applicable.description: Step slugs the founder ruled out — the "not_applicable" list of marketinque.json. Free tier only; ignored for a project.

last_done.description: Free tier: when each recurring step was last done, { "<slug>": "YYYY-MM-DD" } — the "last_done" map of marketinque.json. Steps that repeat come due again from this date. A project uses its own dates.

tools.name: record_outcome
tools.description: Record the founder’s answer to “did it work?” for a play or plan step they ran: worked, some or nothing, and how many weeks since it shipped. Only from the founder’s own words, after it has run two weeks or more; never your guess. whats_next and next_steps list what is due (outcomes_due, ask_outcomes). Answers are pooled across everyone who uses marketinque and shown per play once three different founders have answered, so the next founder learns what works; the note is never shown. A later answer replaces an earlier one.

slug.description: A play slug, or the plan step slug it was run as.

verdict.description: worked: it moved the number it was for · some: a little, or not enough to keep doing · nothing: no visible effect.

stage.description: The product’s stage when it ran.

traits.description: Product traits that decide which steps apply (b2b, b2c, ai-native, dev-tool, no-code, mcp, has-integrations, eu-traffic, mobile-app); omit for the generic plan. Free tier only; a project's saved traits are used instead.

note.description: What moved, in the founder’s words (kept private).

tools.name: list_directories
tools.description: Places that give a startup a backlink, one phase at a time in the order that works. Default phase bl-sprint: the 95 free, dofollow, page-scoped, graded rows. Each row carries its submission page (or where to find it) and, for a project, the listing already recorded.

phase.description: bl-sprint (default) · bl-reach (free, nofollow/host-scoped) · bl-paid · bl-optional · bl-tail

category.description: Filter by the catalog category, e.g. "AI Tools", "Software Reviews".

min_dr.description: Only rows with at least this domain rating (0–100).

unrecorded_only.description: Project only: skip rows already recorded — listed, submitted or skipped. The next batch, in one call.

offset.description: Rows to skip, for paging past `limit`.

tools.name: get_directory
tools.description: One directory from the index: domain rating, dofollow, price, category, the submission page URL (or where to look for it), account_required (the page redirected to a sign-in when probed — most rows want a sign-in at submit anyway), founder_fills (a form an agent cannot drive), the note from the last session that worked it, and — for a project — the outcome already recorded. Read the note before opening the page. Read-only.

tools.name: get_submission_kit
tools.description: What every directory form asks for, written once. A project returns its product profile and brand dossier plus the state of the five kit steps; anonymous callers get the five steps to draft from the product site.
